# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–7 (Complete and Final – Updated 81)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, Wilhaven, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, hill farms of Coldcombe, Humdrum Hall, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Prince Regent locations, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, hill farms of Fenmere, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Hants, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village, Bloomsbury, Russell Square, Harrowgate
- **Narrative Presence**: Narrator warns Vanity Fair is "a very vain, wicked, foolish place, full of all sorts of humbugs and falsenesses and pretensions"; observes human hearts and self-deceptions with ironic sympathy

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy; mother French opera-girl
- Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; white slender fingers
- Skilled musician, linguist, artist; speaks French with purity; proficient in globes
- Determined, observant, capable of calculated charm; "I might go farther, and fare worse"; speaks with slight foreign accent when agitated/discussing maternal relatives
- **Governess at Queen's Crawley**: Governess to Rose and Violet; manages household; writes Sir Pitt's letters; won Miss Crawley's heart; made herself indispensable; Sir Pitt's letters now uncorrected, books unmade up, household business neglected without her
- **Current Role in London**: Companion and nurse to Miss Crawley at Park Lane residence; successfully nursed Miss Crawley during illness; displaced Miss Briggs and Mrs. Firkin from nursing duties; controls sickroom access; maintains composed, fresh appearance despite demanding care; never out of temper; alert, light sleeper with clear conscience; tells stories for entertainment value
- **Nursing Achievements**: Watched Miss Crawley's bedside with indomitable patience; nothing escaped her notice; found use for everything; Miss Crawley improved rapidly; told imitations of Miss Briggs' grief cheering patient; doctors admired improvement; spent weary fortnight in sickroom; nerves of iron
- **Miss Crawley's Gifts and Plans**: Miss Crawley gave Rebecca new gowns, old necklace and shawl; shows friendship by abusing intimate acquaintances to Rebecca; meditates vaguely on future benefits—marry her to Clump the apothecary, settle her advantageously, or return her to Queen's Crawley when season ends
- **Relationship with Amelia**: During Hampshire stay, eternal friendship suffered considerable diminution as both girls occupied with own affairs; Rebecca's part in reunion embrace performed with "perfect briskness and energy" while Amelia blushed, feeling guilty of coldness; first interview brief—Amelia leaving for walk when Miss Crawley arrived in carriage in Russell Square to fetch Rebecca
- **Current Status**: Indispensable to Miss Crawley; not formally installed but accepted as service-giver; Miss Briggs' position now sinecure and derision; Rebecca irreplaceable while useful; has won over Rawdon, Miss Crawley, Mrs. Bute, and now captured Miss Crawley's affection for Amelia through introduction

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood" or dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; household troops around Prince Regent; fought three bloody duels; very large, six feet high; generous with money; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate
- Miss Crawley almost adopted him; disliked Mr. Pitt; always paid his dueling debts; designated for fifty thousand pounds in will per Rector
- **Love for Rebecca**: Completely victimized after six weeks of proximity; made confidante of Mrs. Bute Crawley; barbed shaft of love penetrated his dull hide; raves about her in uncouth convulsions; Mrs. Bute perceives folly, warns him against trifling with artless girl's affections as Miss Crawley loves Sharp like daughter
- **Campaign and Rejection**: During "little campaign" of skirmishes with Rebecca: she was brilliant and lively after drives with Miss Crawley but took no notice of his hints, nods, clumsy expostulations; perpetual defeats; "Crawley heavy cavalry maddened by defeat, routed every day"; Rebecca deflected his advances with dignity and claims of Montmorency breeding
- **Recent Activity**: Heard from Miss Crawley about Amelia; burst into horse-laugh and explained he won two hundred pounds from George Osborne at billiards at Cocoa-Tree; claimed Osborne is young flat who'd have played for anything that day but Captain Dobbin carried him off; dutifully comes to partake of aunt's chicken
- **Mrs. Bute's Warnings**: Mrs. Bute advised him to return to regiment and London; admitted Rebecca is "most clever, droll, odd, good-natured, simple, kindly creature in England"; warned he would not play with poor artless girl's feelings as Miss Crawley would never pardon him
- **Recognition of Plot**: When Mrs. Bute gave him opportunity to see Rebecca at Rectory and walk home with her, Rawdon perceived manifest intention to captivate him; light dawned on his dusky soul; gave prodigious whistle in astonishment; couldn't deny intention; noticed his father's evident liking for Miss Sharp; walked home curling mustachios, convinced he found clue to Mrs. Bute's mystery

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; disliked Mr. Pitt; very attached to Rawdon; adores imprudent matches
- **Nursing and Recovery**: Taken ill; improved rapidly under Rebecca's care; took medicines only from Rebecca's hand; became quite cheerful; loves Sharp like daughter; would never pardon Rawdon for trifling with her
- **Current Relationship with Rebecca**: Quite overcome by little governess; orders Rebecca sit at dinners; demands her presence; gave new gowns, old necklace and shawl; shows friendship by abusing intimate acquaintances; meditates future benefits for Rebecca; accepts Rebecca's service as due; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces; comfortable with Rebecca's presence
- **Suspicion and Insight**: Has lurking suspicion that nobody does anything for nothing; if she measured own feeling towards world, could gauge world's feeling towards her; reflected it is ordinary lot to have no friends if they care for nobody—CLAIM based on her reflection
- **Amelia and New Friendship**: Visited Russell Square, Bloomsbury, John Sedley's house; captivated by Amelia's "sweet blushing face"; praised her complexion and voice; wanted Rebecca to send for her to Park Lane; talked of Amelia with rapture multiple times that day; mentioned her to Rawdon

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome brother of Amelia Sedley; believed infatuated with her; jolly, sociable; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports, song, parade; adored by men; famous drinker and sparrer; won Garrison cup
- Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; shot Captain Marker in duel; robbed young Lord Dovedale at Cocoa-Tree; reputation as "regular Don Giovanni"
- **Engagement to Amelia**: Engaged; admitted to Dobbin and Mrs. Major O'Dowd; furious upon learning regiment knows; later apologized; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"; acknowledges "She's faultless"; insists "there's no fun in winning a thing unless you play for it"; claims will reform after marriage; took tender leave of Amelia morning after visiting her house
- **Financial Transaction**: Visited City; saw Mr. Chopper, his father's head man; received document; exchanged at Hulker & Bullock's for pocketful of money; was "much too elated" (timing: coincides with old John Sedley leaving banker's parlour looking dismal)
- **Recent Gambling**: Won two hundred pounds from Rawdon Crawley at billiards at Cocoa-Tree; "would have played for anything that day" before Captain Dobbin carried him off; described as "young flat" by Rawdon

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Rebecca's former schoolfriend at Chiswick; spurned by discriminating sex despite school friendships
- Small, modest, unaffected young creature; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul like violet
- **Relationship with George**: Confirmed engagement; believes deeply in George; innocent and trusting; assumes George's errands at Horse Guards, Chatham, or friend-visiting; assumes he tired to write long letters; loves him completely and trustingly
- **Actual Behavior**: Leaves home daily; dines abroad six days week; neglected twelve Chiswick friends; single subject to think about; made confidante of little Laura Martin; promised Laura would live with her when married
- **Letters to George**: Extraordinarily long and passionate; filled large paper sheets crossed with astonishing perverseness; whole pages of poetry without pity; underlined words with frantic emphasis; repetitive; doubtful grammar; numerous notes followed him; ordered servant deliver privately
- **Recent Reunion with Rebecca**: During brief first interview at Russell Square, came down with kind smiling looks; timid and graceful; impressed Miss Crawley with "sweet blushing face"; blushed kissing Rebecca, thought herself cold to friend; Rebecca's embrace performed with perfect briskness—Rebecca focused on own affairs during Hampshire stay
- **Current Worries**: Unaware of George's financial transaction; worries her poor papa melancholy and Mr. Osborne dark-looking; alarmed at home; sent George tenderest letter with foreboding evil after his money-receiving evening

**Other Characters**
- **Old Mr. Osborne**: Wealthy merchant in tallow trade; puffy, solemn, yellow-faced; warned George against gambling on pain of disinheritance; ordered George to collect money from Mr. Chopper; stated Sedley's affairs look bad; will not have "lame duck's daughter" in family; required Amelia's ten thousand pounds settled
- **Mrs. Bute Crawley**: Amiable; took great fancy to Rebecca; made confidante by Rawdon; perceives his folly; warns appropriately; gave Rebecca opportunities to see Rawdon at Rectory; acknowledged Rebecca's excellent qualities while warning against trifling
- **Miss Briggs**: Displaced by Rebecca; position now sinecure and derision; company now fat spaniel or discontented Firkin; suffered same treatment she inflicted on Mrs. Firkin
- **Mrs. Firkin**: Eliminated from nursing; came downstairs in jealousy; found consolation in Briggs' suffering
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; fears losing sister's legacy; would not permit daughters to lose Rebecca's educational blessings; sent nearly daily franks to Rebecca with urgent prayers for her return and pathetic statements to Miss Crawley about neglected education; letters numerous and show tenor and spelling of distress
- **Captain Dobbin**: Carried off George Osborne from billiards at Cocoa-Tree
- **Old John Sedley**: Observed leaving banker's parlour looking dismal (timing: coincides with George's gain)
- **Amelia's Confidante**: Laura Martin; promised she would live with Amelia when married
- **Red Jovus and Rira Stenworth**: Red Jovus took Rira Stenworth in marriage at Harrowgate before winter out; couple lived in Harrowgate thereafter
- **Jovus Brackwood**: Laughed at story nobody else found funny (connection to Dunholt subplot unclear)

## Critical Facts and Status
- Rebecca indispensable to Miss Crawley; controls household; has won multiple households' allegiance
- Rawdon completely in love with Rebecca; repeatedly defeated in romantic pursuit; recognizes Mrs. Bute's matchmaking scheme
- Miss Crawley has now met and captivated by Amelia through Rebecca's introduction
- George received substantial money from his father; timing coincides with Sedley family financial crisis
- Amelia remains innocent of George's financial transactions and gambling; worries about family troubles instead
- Miss Briggs permanently displaced; her jealousy confirms Rebecca's superiority
- Sir Pitt desperate for Rebecca's return; household suffers her absence
- Rawdon wins money from George at billiards; George addicted to play before Dobbin intervention
